From 6:00 AM September 6 through 6:00 AM September 7, 2026, Yorba Linda experienced an unusually cool, overcast tropical-remnant rainfall event associated with moisture from Hurricane Marie. Periods of light to moderate rain affected the area through much of the day, occasionally becoming steadier as organized bands moved across northern Orange County. By afternoon, Yorba Linda entered a pronounced dry slot, allowing paved surfaces to begin drying even while showers continued elsewhere across the region. Extensive layered cloud cover persisted into the evening, producing a dramatic post-rain sunset before measurable precipitation effectively ended locally. The 24-hour precipitation total was 0.65 inch, which was submitted to CoCoRaHS as the final total for the 6 AM-to-6 AM observation period. Although measurable rain had ended in Yorba Linda, substantial residual cloud cover and lingering showers elsewhere in Southern California early September 7 showed that the broader Marie-related weather event had not yet completely departed the region.
